Because your account points to no advisory or other artifact, it is an assertion citing no evidence: POL-RD-08 directs that it carry no weight and be discarded, and the exoneration question is therefore not an open, untested limb. I considered whether the absent advisory required the case to go to a human under POL-RD-10(5); it does not, because you invoked POL-RD-03 against nothing — no citation at all — and a clause invoked with nothing behind it is not an untested limb. To the rider and to the driver. Trip TRP-00503 was charged at 17.82 SGD. The distance question is settled by the GPS trace, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement: EV-GPS-00503 records 6.81 km against a booked optimal of 4.2 km, an excess of 2.61 km, or 62.14% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%) and, being above 50%, is a material deviation. The driver's answer - that the app chose the road and the passenger should complain to the company - is not a defence under the loaded policy: POL-RD-01 measures the deviation on the trace rather than on fault, and POL-RD-08 requires the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exoneration, which a general assertion about the navigation does not do. No exculpatory clause can run on this record: the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00503-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, the chat log EV-CHAT-00503 holds zero messages, the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled type. The remedy is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which governs because the fare model on EV-FARE-00503 is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). Run on the figures: charged_total 17.82; recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x 1.0 surge read from EV-FARE-00503 + 0.80 platform fee + nil ERP + nil waiting time - nil promo = 9.85; refund = 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded UP to 8.00 payable. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and, at 44.7% of the charge, below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of 8.00. Nothing is added on top: every pass-through line on EV-FARE-00503 is zero (empty erp_gantries, tolls 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00), so POL-RD-09(1) has nothing to correct and POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry or misplaced surcharge, and no billing-integrity referral arises. The material deviation required the driver-profile check under POL-RD-06, but no pattern is established: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the window (ratio 0.0), so there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No driver compensation is owed: the billed 6.8 km matches the trace's 6.81 km to within 0.01 km, far short of the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires. The rider's account of being late for a lesson and of paying 'almost double' is understood, but those are not recoverable heads under this policy; the refund is confined to the excess distance and time over the optimal route. No escalation trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired (175 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gaps), no timestamps invert, and the refund is far below both the 150.00 ceiling and the charged total. Confidence is 0.90; the measurements deciding this ruling come from artifacts at full weight 1.0.

To the rider and to the driver — here is what is settled and what is not, and why this case goes to a human reviewer instead of being paid out or dismissed today.

What is settled. The platform's optimal route between Paya Lebar Square and Tampines MRT is 9.4 km and 14.0 minutes. The GPS trace for the trip records 23.86 km — the trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded 23.9 km under POL-RD-01 — an excess of 14.46 km, or 153.83% of optimal. That clears both establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km absolute) and is a material deviation on this trip's own evidence. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and no jumps, so no independent corroboration is required under POL-RD-07. The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden: the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all carry TRP-00504, her profile's deviation_claims_60d is 0, and no extra corroboration is demanded of her. The fare is METERED, and on the fare breakdown's own constants the optimal-route fare would be 3.80 + (0.75 x 9.4) + (0.28 x 14.0) = 15.57 at the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on that artifact, plus the 0.80 platform fee. Against the 33.17 charged, that is a refund of 17.60 — 53.06% of the charge, above the 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. Nothing is added for pass-throughs: ERP, tolls, surcharge, waiting fee and promo are all nil, so POL-RD-09 contributes nothing further. There was no rider-requested detour (the chat log exists and is empty, so POL-RD-04 cannot run), no amended pickup or dropoff (POL-RD-05 cannot run), the vehicle was RYDE_X so POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the fare was not upfront-quoted so POL-RD-11 does not apply. I have also run the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check that materiality requires: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available and no conduct referral follows. Only those two profile fields were used for that test; the lifetime counters such as prior_deviation_flags are context only and grounded no finding.

What is not settled. The driver's explanation is that a car behind him flashed high beams several times near the exit, that he believed an accident lay ahead so he stayed on the expressway, and that he turned back at the next exit — in the rider's account, he said he thought the road was closed. That is an external-event defence, and the only clause that can carry it is POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming the affected segment with a validity window overlapping the trip. The only advisory artifact in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00504-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it can carry no fact and only its absence is citable (POL-GEN-02(3)). POL-RD-10(5) names precisely this situation — a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory — as one in which no final monetary ruling may issue. The driver's account on its own does not establish a closure: a stated reason records only that it was stated, a record the platform generates is the platform's, and POL-RD-03 reads the advisory rather than the driver's belief, so a general assertion of this kind does not discharge his POL-RD-08 burden. But the absent advisory is a gap in the record, not a finding against him, and the same principle that stops a data failure being turned into a finding for one side stops it being turned into a finding for the other.

Result. The outcome is ESCALATE, which is terminal: no money moves now, both money fields are null, and the disputed 33.17 is held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's arithmetic is not rejected — if the reviewer concludes there was no closure, the POL-RD-02 refund of 17.60 is the figure that follows; if the reviewer concludes the driver's external-event account is made out on a properly produced advisory, exoneration under POL-RD-03 would change that. What would resolve the case is the LTA advisory record for the Paya Lebar–Tampines corridor on the evening of 23 August 2026, or a record confirming that no advisory was issued. My confidence is 0.70, at the platform floor.

To both parties. The route question is settled by the GPS trace, not by the trip record's rounded copy. EV-GPS-00505 measures 30.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the platform's optimal estimate stored on EV-TRIP-00505 is 22.10 km. The excess is 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and also the 8.0 km absolute gate, so this is a MATERIAL deviation. The trace is complete — 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and no jump — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07, nothing need corroborate it, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The driver's own statement ('I went around') does not dispute the route. The driver's fog account does not excuse the deviation. POL-RD-03 exonerates only against a traffic advisory naming a road the optimal route uses, with a window covering the trip. The only advisory in the record is EV-ADVIS-00505-01, which is MISSING — no payload, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and it records that no advisory covered the SLE or TPE in that window. The driver produced no advisory ID and no artifact of his own, so POL-RD-08 applies: a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the burden that shifts to the driver once the rider has shown a qualifying excess on an unimpaired trace. The fog assertion is discarded and the excess stands. I have considered, and do not adopt, the submission that this record must be escalated under POL-RD-10(5). To both parties: this is really two questions, and they come out differently.

THE ROUTE. There was no deviation. The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-00525, trace_distance_km 4.58) against the booked optimal of 4.4 km (EV-TRIP-00525) is an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.09 per cent. CONFIDENCE AND REFERRALS. The deciding fact — that the charge exceeds the quote — is carried by EV-FARE-00525, weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. CLAIMS ANSWERED. The rider's acceptance of the 4.30% figure and her concession that this does not clear the 20% limb are correct and dispose of her POL-RD-02 refund request (5.55) — a deviation is the precondition and it is absent. Her remaining points all hold and are accepted: the artifacts describe one trip (matching TRP-00527 and the 17:21:40 start on trace and trip record); the trace's 60.91 km governs; the pooled baseline is 58.4 km; no chat instruction shifts any distance to her; and her rider_profile counters deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift is not triggered and she is held to no higher standard. The driver's points are accepted: the pooled baseline, the clean trace, the empty chat log, the null amendment fields, the fare lines, and the POL-RD-06 profile check, which the driver clears on the clause's own fields (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, below both the 3-flag and 5%-ratio tests). The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 asks for and is not used — POL-GEN-01 confines that artifact to credibility weighting; it was flagged in the pre-pass and nothing on either profile beyond the clause-named counters has been relied on. No repeat-deviation pattern exists, so POL-RD-06(c) produces no conduct referral.

DISCLOSURE. EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING — no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. A zero-weight artifact carries no fact and its absence is citable; it decides nothing in either direction, since with the excess at 4.30% there is no deviation for a closure to exonerate and, equally, the rider cannot convert its absence into a deviation the trace does not show. It is named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. No other artifact falls below weight 1.0.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The deciding fact — that the excess does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold — is carried by the GPS trace (60.91 km) and the trip record (58.4 km optimal), both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. Confidence is set at 0.90, comfortably above the 0.70 escalation floor, and none of the POL-RD-10(1)-(8) triggers fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, timestamps agree, every charge line has a trace counterpart, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact. This is a ruling, not an escalation, and no clause on this record mandates a referral.

To the rider and to the driver: this dispute is about whether the trip was overcharged through a route deviation. On the evidence it was not, and no money moves.

Distance. Both sides and the record agree on the measurement. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace figure governing: trace_distance_km is 22.26 km against a booked optimal of 22.1 km, an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only if the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms AND 20% of optimal; both gates must pass, and both fail here by more than an order of magnitude. No deviation is established, and the clause says expressly that where a gate fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. I accept the driver's threshold claims and the rider's own concession of the same arithmetic. The rider's related point — that the charge was metered on the rounded 22.3 km copy rather than the governing 22.26 km trace — does not help: POL-RD-01's non-citation rule governs the threshold test, not the meter, and the 0.04 km difference produces no excess and no refund right.

The fare and the rider's figures. The filed claim speaks of a charge of 91.60 and of 'no surge'. The only fare artifact (EV-FARE-00528, weight 1.0) records total_charged 44.44, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and it carries surge_multiplier 1.4 — POL-RD-02 fixes the surge on fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else. The booking estimate shown was 58-62 before surge, so the charge sits below the estimate, not above it, and the trip was METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 gives no quote-versus-charge difference. The 91.60 figure and the 'no surge' assertion appear in no artifact and cannot carry a finding. The rider's account that a manager already refunded the difference and issued a voucher is equally unsupported: the ledger shows no refund.

The 1.05 the rider asks for. The fare breakdown carries a recomputation pricing the trip at 43.4370 against 44.44 — a difference of 1.0030, rounding to 1.05. That arithmetic is POL-RD-02, and POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. No deviation is established, so the clause never engages and the 1.05 is not a live entitlement; it is what the arithmetic would yield if the gates had been crossed. I decline it, and NO_ACTION leaves the 44.44 charge standing.

Billing integrity. The one route open regardless of deviation — POL-RD-09(4) — gives nothing: there are no ERP gantry lines (ERP total 0.00), no airport surcharge, and every charge line (base fare 3.80, metered distance and time, the 1.4 surge, the 0.80 platform fee) matches this trip's own recorded movement. There is no phantom line to refund.

Exculpation and escalation. The threshold failure decides the case before any exculpatory clause is needed, but I record that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by the driver) and the chat log EV-CHAT-00528 is empty, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-04 could not have been run in any event. The GPS trace is clean — 229 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and no POL-RD-10(3) trigger exists. Reviewing the other escalation triggers: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the timestamps agree (the trace opens 08:16:40 and closes 08:54:40 on the trip's started_at and ended_at); no charge line is unmatched; and the rider's unsubstantiated narrative does not put the two sides on comparable admissible evidence. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so I rule rather than escalate, and no clause produces a referral.

On the rider's request to hold the amount because the record 'does not agree' on the payment state: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative, and on this rider-filed dispute it leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand. An unrecorded earlier conversation is not evidence of a refund and does not change the ruling on this trip. If the platform wishes to look into that earlier support exchange, that question belongs to a human reviewer; it is not a clause-mandated referral and it does not hold the disputed amount.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charge of 44.44 stands, no refund is due to the rider and no compensation to the driver, and no referral arises. Confidence 0.90, resting on the GPS trace and trip record, both at weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The fare stands and no money moves. This was a 2.5 km booking (ION Orchard to Great World) on a METERED taxi fare, and the platform's own GPS trace measures the driven route at 2.61 km — 0.11 km, or 4.4%, more than the booked optimal of 2.5 km. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal. Both gates fail (0.11 < 0.8; 4.4% < 20%), and POL-RD-01 requires the governing figure to be the trace, not the rounded 2.6 km convenience copy on the trip record — the result is the same on either. No deviation being established, POL-RD-02 never runs, so the conditional refund arithmetic in the fare breakdown (recomputed fare 12.0750, refund before rounding 4.2750, payable 4.30) is not payable. There is likewise no billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4): the fare carries no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so there is no phantom line to correct. On the rider's request for ESCALATE: POL-RD-10(5) fires only where a party invokes an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool. The driver invoked no exculpatory clause here and needed none, because no deviation was ever established and the driver's burden under POL-RD-08 never arose; a bare assertion that traffic was bad, citing no evidence, is discarded under POL-RD-08's burden rule, and a discarded assertion is not an escalation ground. POL-RD-10(1) does not fire either: the facts this ruling rests on — the GPS trace, the trip record and the payments ledger — are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, and all three carry trip_id TRP-00529 with consistent timestamps, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor. The only impaired artifact, traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is citable, as both sides rightly say, but it carries no fact and this ruling does not rest on it. Both profiles were used only for the tests their clauses name (deviation_claims_60d on the rider's side, deviation_flags_90d/completed_trips_90d on the driver's); neither party's rating, account age, lifetime trips or cancellation rate was used, and the rider's own claim that the rating field is context-only is correct.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both of you, and I want to be straight about what this forum can and cannot do.

THE FARE (SGD 27.90). This was an upfront-quoted trip (RYDE_X, EV-FARE-00531). The quoted fare was SGD 27.90 and the amount charged on the platform was SGD 27.90, so charged_over_quote is 0.00 — nothing was added over the quote. The only other possible lines are the airport surcharge, recorded at SGD 0.00, and ERP/tolls, recorded at SGD 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges are fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available on an upfront-quoted trip, and there is no pass-through line to correct. The platform charge of SGD 27.90 is correct and stands.

THE ROUTE. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531), which recorded 15.79 km against an optimal route of 15.50 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%. That fails both POL-RD-01 tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%). The trace is complete (100% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps), so it is not impaired and no corroboration is needed. The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00531-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore carries nothing, and no closure exoneration arises. No route deviation is established.

THE SGD 40. Ms Rider, the SGD 40 you describe is not ignored — it is recorded in the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00531): the driver wrote 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' at 22:49:40 and you replied 'ok sent' at 22:50:40, and the driver's statement confirms he asked and was paid. So the payment is documented and I do not doubt you made it. The difficulty is remedy. The SGD 40 is not a line of the fare breakdown, and this tribunal's refund machinery runs only on fare-breakdown lines. POL-RD-09(4) refunds a charge line for a gantry the trace never crossed, or an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport. This trip DID originate at Changi Terminal 2 (EV-TRIP-00531), and the ledger's surcharge line is SGD 0.00, so there is no wrongly applied surcharge line to refund — the SGD 40 was never a platform charge. No other clause in the loaded policy reaches a private transfer between the two of you, and POL-GEN-03 lets money move only as a fare refund or a platform payment to the driver. So the SGD 40 cannot be ordered returned in this forum, and I have not manufactured a referral to do it: a referral exists only where a clause produces one, and none does here (POL-RD-06(c) requires a material deviation and an established pattern, neither of which exists; POL-RD-09(4) requires a billing-integrity defect on the ledger, which does not exist).

ON ESCALATION. POL-RD-10 escalates only on its listed grounds. None is present: confidence is above 0.70; all identifiers match TRP-00531; the trace is unimpaired; the timestamps agree (started 22:51:40, ended 23:13:40 on both trip record and trace); no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; any refund is zero, not above SGD 150 or the charged total; the evidence is consistent rather than two-sidedly contradictory; and every fare line has a counterpart. So this is not an escalation case, and the disputed sum is not held.

WHAT I CAN SAY PLAINLY. The driver's in-app message that the airport surcharge 'cannot' go through the app does not match this platform's fare model, under which the airport surcharge is a platform line (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak on a trip originating at Changi) and the platform charged none on this trip. The SGD 40 was collected off-platform and is outside what this fare-dispute process can order returned; if you wish to pursue it, that is a matter for the platform's trust-and-safety channel or between the two of you. On the money in this case, the outcome is NO_ACTION: the SGD 27.90 platform charge stands as charged and correct, and no refund or driver compensation issues.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver.

WHAT IS REFUNDED. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00532) shows an upfront quote of SGD 75.00 and a total charged of SGD 81.00. The SGD 6.00 difference is a single ERP line for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry, and that line is refunded in full. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00532) never comes within the 250 m crossing radius of that gantry — its closest of 289 fixes is 1,159.02 m away — so the gantry is unmatched and the charge is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refundable whether or not any deviation is established. The same SGD 6.00 is the amount by which the 81.00 charged exceeds the 75.00 quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 (there are none, because the one ERP line was not crossed), so POL-RD-11(a) yields the identical figure; nothing is counted twice and nothing is added on top. Refund: SGD 6.00 of the SGD 81.00 contested. The driver did not resist this line and the rider's 'no gantry, I watched' is borne out by the trace.

WHY THERE IS NO DISTANCE OR TIME REFUND. On the governing trace the trip covered 31.49 km (EV-GPS-00532) against a booked optimal of 28.0 km (EV-TRIP-00532) — an excess of 3.49 km, or 12.46%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% of optimal and 0.8 km; the absolute limb passes but the percentage limb does not, and both must pass, so no deviation is established. The rounded trip-record figure of 31.5 km may not be cited for that test and would not change the result. Independently, EV-FARE-00532 records an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, and POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking and bars any distance-or-time refund however large the excess. The rider's complaint that a second passenger was collected does not move any figure: this is a RYDE_X trip, not a pooled product, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary analysis is not engaged, and the whole measured excess is below the threshold in any event. The rider's comparison with other riders' refunds is not evidence about this trip; each case is decided on its own record.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's statement that 'local roads were faster that day' carries no weight. No traffic advisory supports it — the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00532-01, is missing, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, a blocking admissibility defect), and its absence is itself citable — and an unsupported general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge the driver's burden (POL-RD-08). Because no deviation was established, no exoneration clause (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05) had to be reached, and none of them can restore a distance charge that was never refundable. The driver's point that 'the ERP is part of the fare package' does not make chargeable a gantry his vehicle never crossed: pass-through lines are settled on what was actually crossed, not on what the booking engine assumed. The driver's admission that he did not take the expressway, and that the other passenger was 'a short hop', is consistent with the trace but does not alter the amount.

ON THE DRIVER'S POL-GEN-03 FRAMING. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than NO_ACTION: the present state does not stand in full, because part of the contested amount — the unmatched ERP line — is supported by the evidence and is returned.

The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00618, weight 1.0, 205 fixes at 10 s cadence, no gaps) places you inside the 150 m Changi T3 arrival radius from 15:03:50 to 15:12:40 — a single continuous in-geofence hold of 530 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum — and your 'arrived' tap at 15:03:52 follows the first qualifying fix, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) and POL-NS-02 are met, and limb (c) is met with 50 seconds to spare (derived shortfall minus 50 s, i.e. a surplus). POL-NS-05 does not catch you: no false-arrival marker exists, and POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to work on. But arrival is not the case you have to make; a no-show is. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (d) requires the trip to have been terminated by you with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT at or after the dwell elapsed. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00618, weight 1.0) shows the opposite: status COMPLETED, cancelled_at null, cancelled_by null, cancellation_reason_code null, with the meter running 15:12:50 to 15:34:40 over 16.5 km from Changi T3 to Paya Lebar Square. The passenger boarded and you drove him. No no-show occurred, so no cancellation fee arises, and POL-NS-07 pays you 80 percent of that fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full — it is not. The SGD 4.80 you seek (80 percent of the SGD 6.00 AIRPORT zone fee) is therefore not payable, and the fare breakdown's own money block (EV-FARE-00618, weight 1.0) computes your compensation at SGD 0.00. The anti-farming guard does not trip on your profile — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 110 completed trips, a rate of 0.009, both below the thresholds of 4 and 0.08 — but that is moot, because the entitlement never arises. Your own submission concedes the point, noting that the record does not show a termination on a no-show reason code and that this is 'the one gap' in the case; I agree, and it is decisive. Your assertion in the claim that 'the rules say I get compensated for waiting beyond the minimum' cites no clause in this policy, and no clause in this category creates a waiting payment on a trip that ran to completion.

Rider — there is no contested charge on your ledger for any ruling to move. The fare breakdown itemises cancellation_fee SGD 0.00 and waiting_time_fee SGD 0.00 against total_charged SGD 29.08 (base 3.80 + distance 12.38 + time 6.10 + airport surcharge 6.00 + platform fee 0.80), payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00. Nothing is owed to you and nothing is recoverable from you for a no-show. Your account of the pickup (that you walked your luggage to the car and were told coming to the door was 'not my job') is consistent with a completed trip and is noted, but no clause in this category produces a refund or a referral on it.

Both parties on the subordinate routes: POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider here — the chat log holds zero messages and the rider's 41 fixes sit between about 249 m and 258 m from the pin, outside the 200 m AIRPORT presence radius, so limbs (a) and (c) both fail — but that route was never engaged, since no fee was charged to refund. Referrals: none — no clause here (POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record, POL-NS-07 escalation packet) produces one. The present state stands: the driver's claim is not supported and the charge stands as it presently is. Confidence 0.9, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts (trip record and fare breakdown) that carry the deciding fact.

The controlling finding is that the driver never reached the pickup point. Independently, POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line for a waiting-period shortfall: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. That clause refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responded, so the rider's response does not matter to the refund.

The trace has 100% coverage, no gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell, and no accuracy allowance the policy recognises moves a 263.97 m fix inside a 120 m radius. POL-NS-03 does not engage at all: it requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell at a point within 400 m of the pin, and the trace shows no such hold — the driver was moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h. The driver's request for the POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 therefore fails at the predicate; in any event the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin, which is the limb (i) situation, not limb (ii).

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 both displace it, so the SGD 3.20 figure (80% of SGD 4.00) is never reached, and the anti-farming check is not reached either.

Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap does not bite and the case does not escalate under POL-NS-09.

The 18:04:00 'arrived' marker is a false marker under POL-NS-05, caught by both of its independent triggers: at that timestamp the driver was 377.4 m from the pin (more than 300 m) and moving at 40.6 to 43.5 km/h (above the 15 km/h motion threshold). The waiting clock therefore recomputes to run from a first qualifying in-geofence fix that does not exist anywhere in the trip, and POL-NS-05(ii) requires the fee refunded in full with no compensation payable and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event. POL-NS-02 reaches the same result (no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the 18:09:40 cancellation), as does POL-NS-06 arithmetically (0 seconds measured against 300 seconds required). The 5.7-minute wait_time_min in the trip record is measured from the false marker and cannot cure the defect.

THE DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS. (1) Compensation under POL-NS-07 is not payable: it is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check was correctly read as not tripping — no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 110, a ratio of about 0.009, so neither the count limb nor the rate limb is met — but that only means nothing withholds a payment that never arises. (2) The fare line is not defective: SGD 4.00 is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) does not disturb the amount. That finding does not make the charge lawful. (3) The escalation argument under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected. There is no unresolved conflict: the apparent tension between the trip record's arrival event and the trace is exactly what POL-NS-05 decides, by deeming the marker false and recomputing the clock, and POL-NS-08(a) finds no clock skew (the 18:04:00 marker coincides with a trace fix, so the skew is well inside 90 seconds). (4) POL-GEN-03's rule that NO_ACTION leaves the charge in place does not apply, because the rider's case displaces the charge.

THE RIDER'S ARGUMENTS. The refund does not depend on rider exoneration. POL-NS-04 is not engaged: limb (a) fails because her only message ('what? no. I'm getting out at the petrol station') refuses an off-platform cash demand rather than locating her, and limb (c) fails because her six fixes sit 319.2 to 321.8 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Her account of being carried in the car is also not supported by the trace she brings (her device reports 0.0 km/h at 320 m from the pin while the vehicle moves at 40 km/h and above). None of that matters here: the refund rests on the driver's own trace, not on the rider's narrative. Her point that the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code cannot bear limb (d) is correct — the code alone does not establish that a required dwell had elapsed, and the platform, not the driver, terminated the trip.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The deciding facts — zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a false arrival marker — are carried by EV-GPS-00625 at weight 1.0, corroborated by EV-TRIP-00625 at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and no deciding fact rests on discounted evidence. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires (confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the conflict is clause-resolved; the counterparty dispute counters are 0 and 0; the anti-farming check does not trip and no_show_disputes_30d is 0; no sole impaired evidence). The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00625-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is cited only for its absence, makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, and decides nothing. The case is therefore decided rather than escalated.

NOTED FOR THE RECORD, NOT REFERRED: the driver's in-app message demanding 'ERP 25 each cash' has no counterpart in the priced ledger (tolls_erp 0.00, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and his own statement concedes he combined two bookings in one vehicle. The only clause-mandated referral this case produces is the false-arrival record under POL-NS-05(ii).

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold — neither collected from the rider nor refunded — while review is pending. Here is why, for both of you.

WHAT IS SETTLED. The charge turns on POL-NS-01, which is conjunctive: the SGD 4.00 fee stands only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) — a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record — is satisfied on the platform's own record (12:26:40). Limb (d) — no boarding, terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — is satisfied (cancelled_at 12:35:40). Those two limbs are decided in the driver's favour.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. Limbs (b) and (c) are read off the GPS trace. Limb (b) requires the trace to place the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before 12:26:40; limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, expressly NOT from the 'arrived' tap. EV-GPS-00626 is MISSING: the admissibility pre-pass records issue MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight_multiplier 0.0 — 'No driver telemetry was retained for this trip.' There is no GPS evidence at all.

RIDER'S ARGUMENT (limb (b) fails, POL-NS-02 full refund): REJECTED. An absent trace is the limiting case of an impaired one, and POL-NS-08(b) makes a trace with fewer than six fixes across the waiting window impaired. POL-NS-02's 'no qualifying in-radius fix' rule addresses a trace that was kept and shows the driver elsewhere; the clause's own note says a trace too poor to support the arrival test is impairment rather than proof of absence, and that applies with more force where no trace was kept. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore UNDECIDED — not proof the driver arrived, and not proof he did not. An undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail.

DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS: (1) The recorded wait of 9.0 minutes (12:26:40 to 12:35:40, wait_time_min 9.0) is REJECTED as the statutory dwell: limb (c) runs the clock from GPS geofence entry, not from the driver's tap. (2) The missing trace cannot be run affirmatively against the driver — accepted as far as it goes, but it cuts both ways: the same absence means the fee cannot be carried either. (3) The driver's counterparty statement ('I had gone offline for a break… I never accepted it knowingly') is an admission against his own interest that he was not attending the pickup, and it leaves the 12:26:40 'arrived' marker unexplained; it does not, however, supply the GPS position the limbs require. (4) POL-NS-04 does not apply — the chat log is COMPLETE but empty, and the driver's in-app call at 12:32:40 was answered — and the rider correctly concedes this. (5) POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING. (6) POL-NS-07 compensation of SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00) is REJECTED: it is payable only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied IN FULL, and limb (b) is not; the anti-farming check itself passes (no_show_terminations_30d 1, 1/110 = 0.009, below both thresholds of 4 and 0.08), which clears the withholding branch but creates no entitlement. So is the POL-NS-03 pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 — the 400 m stationary test cannot be run without a trace.

LEDGER AND INTEGRITY. No POL-NS-08(d) defect: the SGD 4.00 charged equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

WHY ESCALATE. The only evidence that could decide arrival is the missing trace at weight 0.0. POL-NS-08 so provides (ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND, case escalates under POL-NS-09), POL-NS-09(e) fires because the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired, and POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.0 — below the 0.70 floor — engaging POL-NS-09(a) as well. Escalation is terminal and replaces the money outcome. The profile triggers do not fire (disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 for both parties under POL-NS-09(c); rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 under POL-NS-09(d)). No clause produces a referral on these facts.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER: obtain the driver telemetry for TRP-00626 (or other evidence of the driver's position between 12:26:40 and 12:35:40) and determine whether he was inside the 50 m STANDARD radius for a continuous 300-second dwell. If he was, the SGD 4.00 stands and POL-NS-07 compensation may follow; if he was not, or the trace genuinely does not exist, decide the fee on the balance of the remaining evidence, noting the driver's own admission that he was offline and did not knowingly accept the trip.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties. The SGD 6.00 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00627 is refunded in full to the rider; no driver compensation is payable.

WHY THE FEE CANNOT STAND. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold. The driver's 'arrived' event (limb (a)) and the driver-side RIDER_NO_SHOW termination (limb (d)) are on the trip record, and the Driver Advocate expressly does not contend limbs (b) and (c) are made out. On the platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00627, weight_multiplier 1.0, COMPLETE: 79 fixes at 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps), the vehicle never came closer than 623.57 m to the Clarke Quay pin (mean 822.99 m; worst 1,625.98 m) between 23:10:40 and 23:23:40, and it was travelling at 28.1-30.6 km/h. qualifying_fix_count is 0, run_count is 0 and the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum for LARGE_VENUE. Limbs (b) and (c) both fail, and because the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before the 23:24:10 cancellation, POL-NS-02 gives the rider a full refund of the fee.

THE DRIVER ADVOCATE'S CONTRARY ARGUMENTS FAIL. (1) Limbs (a) and (d) alone cannot carry the fee; all four are required, and two are conceded absent. (2) The POL-NS-09(b) escalation is rejected: that limb fires only where NO clause resolves the cross-source conflict, and POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 make the GPS trace the arrival test (with POL-NS-05 the false-marker test), which resolves the conflict in one direction and leaves no open question. No other POL-NS-09 trigger fires. (3) The POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0, not 0.4: the deciding fact — that the driver never entered the geofence — is carried by EV-GPS-00627 at weight 1.0, and the ruling does not rest on the trip record. EV-TRIP-00627 is impaired (weight_multiplier 0.4, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (MAJOR)); its arrived_at of 23:15:10 and 9.0-minute wait_time_min are precisely the contradicted figures and are outweighed by the trace; per POL-GEN-02(3) the finding survives the discount because it does not depend on that artifact. (4) Driver compensation is refused: POL-NS-07 pays 80% of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied IN FULL, which it is not, so the SGD 4.80 computed in the fare_breakdown's derived block is not emitted. POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route is unavailable — it needs stationary dwell within 400 m of the pin, and the nearest approach was 623.57 m with no stationary interval, and registered_pickup_points is 1, so there is no pin-ambiguity goodwill either. The driver's account ('no parking, I circled') is what the trace shows: circling at 28-30 km/h up to 1.6 km away, with no advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-00627-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) cannot make the separate stretches summable. (5) The rider's message 'no, you cancel' is not a locating or coordinating message, so POL-NS-04 does not apply; the refund does not depend on it. The rider's own device telemetry (64 qualifying fixes, mean 12.90 m from the pin, max 17.62 m) confirms the rider was at the pin throughout.

THE AMOUNT. The SGD 6.00 is the fee_schedule resolution-rule figure — the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (SGD 6.00) — and reconciles with the fare_breakdown cancellation_fee line, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The entire contested sum of SGD 6.00 is returned.

CONFIDENCE. The ruling rests on EV-GPS-00627 (weight 1.0) for the non-arrival and zero dwell, and on EV-FARE-00627 (weight 1.0) for the amount; the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is therefore 1.0, and confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor shared by POL-NS-09(a) and POL-GEN-02.

REFERRAL. Under POL-NS-05(ii): the 'arrived' marker was set while the trace placed the vehicle more than 300 m out and moving above 15 km/h, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, so the trip is to be recorded as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-32752. This referral rides with the refund and does not displace it.
